thread.title: Special Participation E: Claude Study "Buddy"
thread.content: I used Claude's study feature to use it as a study "buddy". I pretended to be studying for an exam, trying to review content, and study for a specific topic via pre-lecture notes all using Claude to guide my studies.I started out with this map to see if it could connect all the topics from this class into a graph and assess the relationships between them. Below is the trace with all my comments! Hope this is helpful and happy studying.
thread.document:
I used Claude's study feature to use it as a study "buddy". I pretended to be studying for an exam, trying to review content, and study for a specific topic via pre-lecture notes all using Claude to guide my studies.

I started out with this map to see if it could connect all the topics from this class into a graph and assess the relationships between them. Below is the trace with all my comments! Hope this is helpful and happy studying.

comments.content: <document version="2.0"><paragraph>Very interesting. <break/><break/>Notice how it can't possibly track scope with what we are teaching. For example,  it mentions LSTMs --- which we didn't cover because they have been entirely subsumed by the Mamba-style of state-space models --- and it also teaches you archaic absolute position embeddings even though we've decided to basically only mention them so as to focus on RoPE and NoPE which work much better in practice, along with learned relative positional embeddings which are useful pedagogically as a bridge to RoPE. <break/><break/>The interesting question with all of these "help-me-study" efforts is how to get proper alignment to the course itself. </paragraph></document>
comments.document:
Very interesting. 

Notice how it can't possibly track scope with what we are teaching. For example,  it mentions LSTMs --- which we didn't cover because they have been entirely subsumed by the Mamba-style of state-space models --- and it also teaches you archaic absolute position embeddings even though we've decided to basically only mention them so as to focus on RoPE and NoPE which work much better in practice, along with learned relative positional embeddings which are useful pedagogically as a bridge to RoPE. 

The interesting question with all of these "help-me-study" efforts is how to get proper alignment to the course itself.
